dedupe_keys.name: european funds for flood protection measures in smolyan bulgaria climate adapt case study

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Smolyan municipality in Bulgaria protected its Ustovo neighbourhood after the Cherna River flooded it in August 2005, when 156 mm fell in 24 hours. Between June 2011 and June 2013 the riverbed was widened and cleaned and flood walls were reinforced and built, for about 477,000 euros, mostly from the EU Regional Development programme; further works followed in 2017 to 2022 under Interreg Greece-Bulgaria. The municipality cleans the riverbed twice a year, and the works are meant to last at least 100 years. Coverage is the city of Smolyan. The page is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, published in 2023 and updated in 2026. Caveats: the benefits were not quantified, and the evidence of success is one wet year (2014) in which the protected district stayed dry. Simulation uses: an example of small-scale river flood defence works and their funding for adaptation planning. Related records: the Prague flood protection case study (case_study-prague-vltava-flood-protection-system).
name: European funds for flood protection measures in Smolyan, Bulgaria (Climate-ADAPT case study)
outcomes: After the works the Ustovo district, flooded in 2005, was not affected in the very wet year 2014, while other neighbourhoods flooded.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study with Smolyan Municipality
resources_used: ERDF Regional Development and Interreg Greece-Bulgaria funding
